div.head: Wi 27[a]
div.ab: Gif þeuw stele ⁊ hi man alese: LXX scll', swa hweder swa cyning wille;
Gif þeuw stele ⁊ hine man alese, LXX scll', swa hweder swa cyning wille;
Gif þeuw stele ⁊ hi[ne] man alese: LXX scƚƚ, swa hweder swa cyning wille.
Wenn ein Sklav stiehlt und man ihn auslöst, [koste dies] 70 Schll., je wie der König entscheidet;
If a slave steals and he is redeemed, [this costs] 70 shillings, as the king decides;
If a slave steals, and is released, 70 shillings [shall be paid]—whichever the king wishes.
If a slave steals and is redeemed, [this is to be at] 70 shillings, whichever the king wishes. If he is killed, half is to be paid for him to the possessor.
If a slave steals and a person redeems him: 70 shillings, whichever the king wants.

note.seg: Aus der möglichen Todesstrafe und dem Zusammenhang folgt Handhaftigkeit auch hierfür
That the thief was caught in the act here too follows from the possible death penalty and from the context
Der Zahlende ist der Herr; denn der Sklave hat weder Sippe noch 70 Schilling, über diese s. Gl unfrei 7
The one who pays is the lord; for the slave has neither kindred nor 70 shillings; on the latter see Gl unfrei 7
Die Endung -ne (s. d. Wb 154) ward durch ∼ über vorhergehenden Buchstaben abgekürzt; das Zeichen übersah dann der Abschreiber.
The ending -ne (see that word in Wb 154) was abbreviated by ∼ over the preceding letter; the copyist then overlooked the sign.

Diese Stellung der Entscheidung zwischen die beiden Alternativen zeigt ungelenken Stil. Eine Textlücke mit Früheren anzunehmen ist nicht nötig. Schwerlich darf Verkauf über See aus 26 ergänzt werden: er war nicht für jeden Sklaven Strafe, bes. nicht für über See Entstammte

This placing of the decision between the two alternatives shows a clumsy style. There is no need to assume a lacuna in the text, as earlier editors did. Sale overseas can hardly be supplied from 26: it was not a punishment for every slave, esp. not for those who came from overseas

note.label: hine
note.note: The number 1 is printed 2 times on the page (27[a], 27[b]), with one footnote.

note.seg: The alternative is given, awkwardly enough, in the following sentence.

note.label: wishes
note.seg: This law is awkwardly expressed if the alternative is the death-penalty. But some alternative price of redemption may perhaps have been accidentally omitted.

note.label: possessor
note.seg: Presumably the man who captured him.

note.label: man
note.seg: Both here and in §22.1, himan is run together, eliminating the ending on the pronoun. Liebermann, Gesetze, 3:30, restores both of these as the accusative hine, and suggests that perhaps originally there was a ~ nasal extension mark over the hi which the copyist overlooked. We might also emend the last phrase þam agende him man healfne agelde, ‘one should pay the owner half for him,’ which grammatically is far preferable. But see the parallel (without the awkward intrusion) in §21; the double accusative construction, however, works better with age than with agelde.

note.label: wants.
note.seg: That is, fine or death. See under ‘Theft’ in Commentary.
